evidence: The original test patched `main_memory.limit` and then only called `Settings.from_env`, which never calls `memory.limit()`, so the patch could not affect the outcome. The agent took the reviewer's 'restructure' option, but that restructure removed the patch from the parse entirely, and F4 shows it still could not catch a refusal moved into `from_env`.
guidance_note: When making a test's setup load-bearing, run the regression it names (move the refusal into `from_env`) and see the test go red before claiming 'it goes red if...' in the docstring.

evidence: The docstring said `create_app` logs the consulted file, and the reviewer correctly noted that no such logging existed, so an unreadable limit file read silently as unconfined. Commit 94785b8 split `FileNotFoundError` from other `OSError` and added a WARNING inside `limit()`, which fixes the real gap rather than just the comment.
guidance_note: Before writing a docstring that names a safety net in another module (`create_app` logs...), grep for that call and confirm it exists.

evidence: `_app` now calls `unsized(settings)`, which reads the real cgroup, and conftest clears `ELVENSPEAK_CONCURRENT_SYNTHESES`, so on a confined runner the existing build tests would refuse before reaching `Catalog`. The autouse `_unconfined` fixture is the right shape. It was inserted at the wrong spot (F7), and it interacted with F1's restructured test (F4).
guidance_note: When a composition-root change adds a read of host state, add the suite-wide stub in the same commit as the feature and list which existing tests would otherwise inherit host state.

evidence: In 94785b8 the F1 fix removed the patch and passed `confined` only to the standalone `unsized()` call, so `from_env` runs under conftest's UNCONFINED stub, and its docstring claims it 'goes red if the refusal is ever moved into from_env', which is false. In 4022351 the agent moved the patch before `from_env` and confirmed by simulating the regression.
guidance_note: A test that claims to catch a specific regression gets that regression applied once, temporarily, before the fix commit is pushed.

evidence: The F2 fix (94785b8) added a test that makes a file unreadable with `chmod(0o000)`. The gitea runner runs as root, so the read would succeed and the assertion would fail in CI. `tests/test_voices.py` already documented this trap and used a directory instead, and the agent confirmed both citations before switching to `mkdir()` in 4022351.
guidance_note: Before writing an 'unreadable file' test, grep the suite for an existing unreadable-file fixture; here test_voices.py already said chmod 000 does not work on the root runner.

evidence: This duplicates F5 on the same line of the test the F2 fix added (chmod 000 under a root runner). It was handled by the same `mkdir()` change in 4022351.
guidance_note: Before writing an 'unreadable file' test, grep the suite for an existing unreadable-file fixture; here test_voices.py already said chmod 000 does not work on the root runner.

evidence: The 94785b8 diff for conftest.py inserts `@pytest.fixture(autouse=True) def _unconfined` directly below the `#:` comment block that documents `_ENVIRONMENT`, which leaves that comment orphaned. The flag names 4022351 (the head at review time), but the fixture landed in 94785b8 as the F3 fix. Moving the fixture below the tuple (a9b647a) was the right fix.
guidance_note: When inserting a new definition into an existing file, check whether the lines immediately above it are a `#:` doc comment for the next symbol, and insert after that symbol rather than between the two.

evidence: Two adjacent comments in settings.py disagree: the `MEASURED_PIPER` comment says the table is quoted in three places, while the field comment says 'four places' and 'not repeated here'. The flag is a false positive: neither 94785b8 nor 4022351 touched settings.py, and the hunk is part of the original PR diff. The reply-hint says pushback, but the reply agrees and a9b647a rewrites both comments.
guidance_note: When centralising a duplicated fact, rewrite every comment that counts or lists its copies in the same edit, and reread them side by side.

evidence: `CONFINED = 2048 MiB` matches the incident figure hardcoded in the refusal's narrative sentence, so `"2048 MiB" in refusal` holds even if the conversion is broken. This is in the original test, not code from a fix commit (4022351 did not touch test_settings.py). The new 3072 MiB test in a9b647a pins the conversion.
guidance_note: When asserting that a rendered message contains a computed value, choose an input whose rendering cannot collide with any literal already in the message template.

evidence: `LIMIT_FILES` read only the mount-root files, which belong to the host under a host cgroup namespace, Nomad exec, or v1. That is a readable but wrong path that reports unconfined with no warning. This is original PR code; a9b647a adds `/proc/self/cgroup` resolution. That fix resolved only the leaf and spawned F12, F13 and F14.
guidance_note: When a module reads a kernel interface to learn a fact about 'this process', write down the namespace/hierarchy semantics (root vs own cgroup, ancestor minimum) before choosing paths, not after a reviewer asks.

evidence: On a 4-core host the default is 8, a substring of '2048'; on 3 cores it is 7, a substring of '1773'. So `str(n) in refusal` cannot detect a missing interpolation. This is original test code, not a fix artifact. The agent asserted on the rendered phrase `({n} here)` and correctly declined the reviewer's tangent about refusing chosen-but-too-wide ceilings.
guidance_note: When asserting that a rendered message contains a computed value, choose an input whose rendering cannot collide with any literal already in the message template.

evidence: The a9b647a diff (the F10 fix) adds `test_no_proc_self_cgroup_falls_back_to_the_roots`. It patches `PROC_SELF_CGROUP` and then passes the same path explicitly to `_candidates`, so the patch is inert. This is the same dead-monkeypatch shape as F1. In 4014af0 the agent found that the suggested fix was still vacuous, and added a test whose patched value changes the answer.
guidance_note: After writing any monkeypatch, delete the patch line once and confirm the test goes red; F1 had already shown this author produces dead patches.

evidence: The F10 fix (a9b647a) added `_candidates` with `except OSError: return LIMIT_FILES`, which silently treats an unreadable `/proc/self/cgroup` like an absent one. That is exactly the absent-vs-unreadable gap the F2 fix had just closed for limit files. The flagged commit 4014af0 only touched tests; the gap came from a9b647a.
guidance_note: When adding a new read of a file to a module that already distinguishes FileNotFoundError from other OSError, apply the same split to the new read; grep the module for `except OSError`.

evidence: The `_own` added in a9b647a returns only the leaf's `memory.max`. Under cgroup v2 the kernel enforces the minimum along the ancestor chain, so a leaf reading `max` under a capped slice reads as unconfined. That is the same silent misdetection one level up. 9da5494 walks the ancestors and takes the minimum, which replaces the ordering rule.
guidance_note: When fixing 'read the wrong cgroup', model the full enforcement rule (minimum over leaf and ancestors) rather than only the specific path the reviewer named.

evidence: The warn-and-continue arm came from the F2 fix (94785b8), and its only test passes a single-element tuple, so `continue` and an early return look the same. This is a coverage gap in that fix. The flag's 4014af0 did not touch it. The agent added a two-candidate test and confirmed the early-return mutation fails it.
guidance_note: When adding a branch whose behaviour is 'keep going', test it with a later element that changes the answer; a single-element input cannot tell continue from return.

narrative: Five reviewed rounds and a sixth that hit the round cap. Rounds 1, 3 and 4 raised only findings caused by the agent's own fixes. The 94785b8 fix commit for F1-F3 produced four findings: a still-vacuous test, a chmod-000 test that breaks on the root runner, and an orphaned comment. The a9b647a fix for the root-vs-own cgroup bug (F10) resolved only the leaf, and three later findings came from it: a dead patch in its new test, an unreadable `/proc/self/cgroup` treated silently, and missing ancestor limits. Every premise was correct and every response was right; the cost was fix quality, not judgment.
guidance_observations: The agent noted in its own reply that this PR had three dead-monkeypatch findings of the same shape; a delete-the-patch-and-see-red check on each new monkeypatch would have prevented all three.

Fix commits added new tests and new reads without applying the module's own established rules (absent-vs-unreadable split, root-safe unreadable fixtures) to them, so each fix opened a fresh instance of a gap already closed.

F10's design flaw (which cgroup answers for this process) went through two partial fixes before the ancestor-minimum rule. Working out the kernel's enforcement semantics up front would have collapsed rounds 3 and 4.

evidence: The aggregate warning was gated on `tightest` being Unconfined, so a task whose own files were read and correctly said `max` was told its files 'do not exist'. fb6d4e1 adds `read_any` and gates on it. That gate later suppressed the warning when a host root was read (F4), and the message text was left saying 'exist' (F3).
guidance_note: Before writing a diagnostic gate, enumerate the input states (absent, unreadable, read-and-max, read-and-number), separately for the own subtree and for the root, and decide the log line for each.

evidence: `_own` builds absolute paths from a hardcoded `/sys/fs/cgroup` root, so patching only `PROC_SELF_CGROUP` and `LIMIT_FILES` left `limit()` reading real host paths. fb6d4e1 also stubs `_own` in that test, and per the reply the agent sealed the other no-argument `limit()` calls as well.
guidance_note: When a test seals a function's inputs, list every absolute path the code under test can construct, not only the module attributes it reads.

evidence: In fb6d4e1 the comment above the warning was changed to 'NOT ONE ... could be read', but the logged message still says 'none of its limit files exist', and a file that exists but raises leaves `read_any` False. The message was already loose before fb6d4e1; the F1 fix rewrote the gate's semantics and comment without bringing the message text along. 914c6d8 changes it to 'could be read'.
guidance_note: When a fix changes what a gate means, reread the log string it guards in the same edit; here the comment was updated and the message beside it was not.

evidence: fb6d4e1 sets `read_any = True` after any successful read, including the `LIMIT_FILES` roots that `_own`'s docstring says belong to the host. So own-file-missing plus root-reads-`max` now suppresses the warning that fired before the F1 fix. The agent renamed it to `read_own`, counting only non-root candidates, in b7571b2.
guidance_note: When adding a flag that summarises a loop over heterogeneous candidates, decide which candidates count as evidence for the question the flag answers, using the module's own trust rules (here: roots are not ours once a subtree is resolved).

narrative: Round 0 found a real false-alarm bug in the aggregate warning (F1) and a hermeticity gap (F2). The F1 fix in fb6d4e1 introduced `read_any`. Rounds 1 and 2 each raised one finding against that flag: the message text left saying 'exist', and the flag counting host-root reads as evidence. Every premise was correct and every acceptance was right; both later rounds came from one incompletely reasoned flag.
guidance_observations: The F1 fix replaced one coarse gate with another without writing out the state table (own vs root, absent vs unreadable vs read). Both later findings are rows of that table.
The agent tested only the reviewer's exact counterexample in each fix; adding the adjacent states (unreadable own file, readable root) in the first fix would have pre-empted rounds 1 and 2.

evidence: The race is real, and the agent concedes it. Holding the socket open would stop the runtime from binding the published port, so that remedy is wrong. Retry-on-bind-failure needs classifying three CLIs' stderr, and the agent showed `container run -p 127.0.0.1::5001` erroring on CLI 1.3.1. The agent says the image-inspect call runs before `_free_port()`; the packet hunk does not show the call order, so that correction is unverified here.

`json.loads(stdout)[0]["variants"][0]["config"]` and `raw["Env"]` raise LookupError/ValueError past `main()`'s `except SmokeFailure`, which contradicts the file's 'one type carrying a sentence' claim. bb159c6 adds one boundary at `_read_config`. The agent's own parametrized test found that `AttributeError` was needed too.
guidance_note: When a file claims every failure reaches the caller as one type, list every parse of external output and wrap it at the boundary when it is written.

evidence: The hunk shows `_print_logs` calling `subprocess.run(..., timeout=CLI_TIMEOUT)` inside `_container`'s `finally` with no `TimeoutExpired` handling. A wedged daemon therefore skips `rm --force` and replaces the original exception. bb159c6 converts the timeout at every site, as the reviewer suggested, using `_run`/`_capture`/`_attempt` so the cleanup calls cannot raise.
guidance_note: Route every subprocess call through one wrapper that owns timeout conversion; a second bare `subprocess.run` beside the wrapper is where the guarantee leaks.

evidence: `match` is 3.10+ syntax, and the script's stated premise is running under whatever `python3` is on PATH. e2281a0 removes the syntax, adds a `feature_version=(3, 8)` parse test that fails on the original commit, and the agent ran the script under macOS's 3.9.6.
guidance_note: For a script documented as running on any system python3, add the feature_version parse test when the script is created, not after review.

evidence: `_capture(argv)` ran before the `try:`, so a `run -d` whose create succeeded and start failed left a named container behind. The agent reproduced the leak with podman. The fix is the reviewer's second option, a sweep in the except path, and it avoids a `started` flag that would print a false 'left behind' warning.
guidance_note: When a context manager claims a leak is unrepresentable, check that the acquiring call itself is inside the region that releases on failure.

narrative: One review round with five findings, all on original code, and a clean approval after. Four were real defects that the agent fixed with live reproduction (the container leak, the 3.9 run). The fifth, the port TOCTOU race, was correctly pushed back with runtime evidence that both suggested remedies were worse. No fix caused a follow-up finding.
guidance_observations: The agent backed both pushback and fixes with executed evidence (a podman leak repro, a container CLI error, a run under python 3.9.6), which is why no fix produced a second round.

evidence: The `case` gave only chatterbox a value, while the comment above it recorded the router failing on `ROUTER_CONSUL_URL` and claimed absent engines 'need nothing'. The agent took the reviewer's second option, a router row stating it is red pending b4h.4, and explained why a stub URL alone would still give /health 503.
guidance_note: When a fix comment cites N observed failures, check the fix addresses all N or names the ones it leaves open.

evidence: The README said CI passes 'whatever a given engine needs', but the workflow supplied nothing for the router. 2111efc qualifies the claim and adds a router paragraph. That insertion stranded the next sentence (F3).
guidance_note: When a fix comment cites N observed failures, check the fix addresses all N or names the ones it leaves open.

evidence: The 2111efc README diff ends the new router paragraph with '...`piper-build-b4h.4`. Running it confined would prove the', so the confinement sentence's 'it' now attaches to the stub container. Instead of the suggested blank line, the agent moved the sentence back to its original paragraph, which restores the antecedent.
guidance_note: When inserting prose into an existing paragraph, insert at a sentence boundary that ends the paragraph, and reread the sentence that now follows the insertion for a changed antecedent.

narrative: Round 0 correctly flagged that the router leg was still red and both the workflow comment and the README claimed otherwise; the agent fixed the documentation and left the leg honestly red. The README fix spliced the router paragraph into the middle of an existing paragraph, which cost round 1 a pronoun-antecedent finding. Round 2 approved.
guidance_observations: The one avoidable round came from a mechanical prose splice in a fix commit; rereading the rendered paragraph after the edit would have caught it.

evidence: `record` returns `{}` for the catalog, so `discovery.engines` never requests the health path and the docstring's 'every target' covers one URL. 349fbb8 returns a tagged service, and the agent reports `asked` now holds both paths, asserted as a set and mutation-checked.
guidance_note: When a fake drives code that branches on the fake's answer, make the fake's answer non-empty enough to reach every path the test claims to cover, and assert the recorded calls exactly.

evidence: Moving `routed()` to tests/fleet.py left five imports unused. The agent confirmed that `ENGINES`' only other occurrence is in a docstring, then deleted all five.
guidance_note: After moving a function out of a file, run a linter for unused imports on the source file before committing.

evidence: This duplicates F1: the catalog stub returning `{}` means `HEALTH_PATH` is never exercised. It was fixed by the same 349fbb8 change, with the mutation check reported.
guidance_note: When a fake drives code that branches on the fake's answer, make the fake's answer non-empty enough to reach every path the test claims to cover, and assert the recorded calls exactly.

evidence: The docstring said 'Four tests'; the agent counted 11 + 1 call sites. It took the reviewer's 'drop the count' option, which removes a number that would go stale again.
guidance_note: Don't put call-site counts in docstrings; state the reason for centralising instead.

evidence: `str(json.load(answer)["base_url"])` turns null into 'None' and 8080 into '8080' without raising, which defeats the function's stated parse-don't-validate purpose. 4b4e6ac checks for a non-empty str, and the agent confirmed null, int and empty string all raise.
guidance_note: When parsing an external JSON field, check its type rather than coercing it with str()/int().

evidence: `_serving_fleet` reused the 180s model-loading `timeout` for a stdlib server that answers in milliseconds, so an unreachable stub costs up to 360s in total. 4b4e6ac adds `FLEET_TIMEOUT = 30.0` and drops the now-dead parameter.
guidance_note: When reusing a timeout constant for a new wait, check that the constant's documented sizing reason applies to the new wait.

narrative: One review round with six findings on original code: two duplicates about a vacuous discovery-path test, dead imports, a stale count, a str() coercion, and a reused timeout. All were real and accepted with correct fixes, some mutation-checked. Round 1 approved with no fix-caused findings.
guidance_observations: Every finding was in the original diff and none followed from a fix; the fixes were verified with mutation or live checks before replying.

evidence: `voice = self.path.split("/")[3]` hardcodes the segment index, so a changed route in speaks.py would yield a wrong voice instead of failing. 373212c matches the whole path and returns 404 otherwise. The agent confirmed that renaming the stream route now fails conformance with 'answered 404'.
guidance_note: When a test fake parses a request, match the whole route shape and reject anything else rather than indexing into it.

evidence: The flakiness concern is real, but the suggested remedy would break the test. The test must both fit `LONGER_TEXT`'s own budget and overrun `TEXT`'s, which caps the ratio near 1.65x, so restoring 3.3x would let a single-budget revert pass. The agent doubled the absolute figures (slack from 0.245s to 0.49s) and kept the ratios, which addresses jitter without losing the test's power.
guidance_note: When shrinking timing constants for a test, size the absolute slack for scheduler jitter, not just the ratio, and record that sizing in the docstring.

narrative: One review round with two findings on original test code. The fake's index-based route parse was rightly replaced with a whole-path match. The flakiness finding got a reasoned different fix that preserves the test's discriminating ratio while adding absolute slack. Round 1 approved.
guidance_observations: The agent's different-fix reply showed with arithmetic why the reviewer's remedy would defeat the test, which is the right way to handle a diagnosis that is real but a cure that is wrong.

evidence: The agent says `piper-build-b4h.scw` is a real lit child with a hashed suffix and that `.5` is a different ticket ('build the real Dockerfile on every ref'). PR #50's title, 'Build and smoke the real Dockerfile on every ref ... (piper-build-b4h.5 ...)', corroborates the `.5` half, so changing the pointer would have mislinked it. The law token decorates a factual correction rather than deciding it.

narrative: A single round with one S1 finding that guessed a hashed lit ticket id was a typo. The agent correctly declined with the ticket's title, and noted the numbered alternative was a different ticket.

evidence: CLAUDE.md restated the chatterbox seconds (624s, 582s, 538.8s) already in the workflow's `prove` comment, and added uncited kokoro/piper/router timings. c1b217b keeps only the ~20-minute figure the warning depends on, points at the workflow comment, and drops the uncited numbers.
guidance_note: When writing a measured figure into a second file, point at the cited source rather than copying it, and don't write numbers without a run citation.

evidence: `prove` now runs all four legs concurrently on every push, and the free-RAM warning addressed only master pushes. That gap is real. The suggested `max-parallel: 1` is weaker than offered, because the file itself records that Gitea ignores the key. ee66e3e documents the concurrency, extends the warning to every push, and cites runs 6272-6274, which ran all four legs with no OOM.
guidance_note: When adding a job that inherits another job's resource profile on a new trigger, carry over its operator warnings to that trigger in the same change.

narrative: One round with two findings on original content: duplicated and uncited measurements in CLAUDE.md, and an unstated concurrency risk on the new `prove` job. The agent pointed at the cited source instead of copying, and declined a no-op `max-parallel` in favour of documenting the real behaviour with run evidence. Round 1 approved.
guidance_observations: The agent rejected a cure the file itself records as ineffective (max-parallel ignored by Gitea) while keeping the diagnosis, which matches the review-findings discipline.
